How debris choices and unsuccessful searches change the PDF

The maps compare the same retained flight and impact trajectories while changing the included evidence. The cruise population starts with 1.02 million candidates, allowing up to 16 turn, 8 Mach and 8 altitude command starts. This remains a model with declared priors. Its validation and that of the combined estimate are unfinished.

The Réunion flaperon pulls southward; Paindane and the Mossel Bay cowling pull northward in these calculations. The new cowling estimates use two independent sets of 4,096 initial ocean paths at each of 77 source locations. The other debris calculations and cruise population are shared.

Different objects included

All six panels use the same current, wave, wind and object-response model. The Réunion-only panel uses its term from this same model. Isotope and Australian coastal non-recovery conditions are omitted throughout. The exterior-only panel omits the Antsiraka cabin and Rodrigues door panels; it is an alternative evidence selection, not a claim that seven objects establish a calibrated likelihood.

After unsuccessful seabed searches

ATSB's reported coverage and detection assessments give an approximate 94% area-average reference. The first row shows weaker effective detection; the second adds the approximate 2018 outline under two overlap assumptions. These are separate conditional models. No region is assigned zero probability in the displayed cases.

Vector PDF · SVG

The update multiplies each impact's existing weight by the chance of missing the aircraft at that location, then normalizes. The updated weight is also assigned to that impact's actual 00:11 parent; the table shows both effects. Overlapping passes within one campaign are counted once. Across campaigns, “shared misses” allows the same terrain or wreckage characteristics to impede both searches; “independent misses” assumes separate detection opportunities.

The 2018 outline is larger than the operator-reported surveyed area. Its optional 60% effective detection combines an approximate coverage allowance and a declared detectability assumption. The recent campaign's area total is not applied spatially because its actual search swaths are not available here.

ATSB (2017), Figure 73, printed p. 96 (PDF p. 105) supplies the 97.4% high-confidence, 2.1% lower-confidence and 0.5% gap fractions. Using 95%, 70% and 0% for their respective detection assessments gives 0.974 × 0.95 + 0.021 × 0.70 = 0.94. Applying it uniformly to the retained data footprint is our approximation; it is not a pointwise sonar-quality map.
